reading.body:
CyrusOne's HOU3-HOU4 campus in Houston publishes 84 MW of IT capacity, making it the largest by disclosed megawattage among Texas facilities tracked here, though most facilities publish no capacity figures at all.

The campus spans 347,000 square feet across two addresses in the 77041 zip code, which works out to approximately 242 watts per square foot of technical space. This power density is consistent with mixed-use colocation serving multiple customer types rather than a dedicated hyperscale facility optimized for single-workload density. At commonly assumed AI training densities of 40 kW per rack, the published capacity would support roughly 2,100 racks, but CyrusOne does not publish deployment assumptions or actual tenant workload composition.

The campus holds Green Globes certification, which addresses building energy efficiency and environmental design. This qualification appeals to tenants with sustainability reporting obligations, but the certification covers none of the factors that determine AI workload readiness: redundancy tier, uptime commitment, power delivery architecture, or cooling strategy. Published spec data does not reveal whether this facility is configured for AI training, inference, other compute workloads, or a mix.

Among the eight Texas facilities with published megawattage figures on this site, HOU3-HOU4 represents 27 percent of disclosed capacity. This ranking reflects both the campus's actual scale and the opacity of most data center operators, who do not publish capacity figures publicly.
